newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to leave hospital on Sunday for a walk.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to leave hospital on Sunday for a walk.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, who underwent heart surgery nearly two weeks ago, plans to leave the hospital where he has been recuperating for a walk on Sunday at a sanatorium outside Moscow, his doctors said.
Russian news agencies quoted Yeltsin's surgeon, Renat Akchurin, as saying Yeltsin would go for an hour's walk at the Barvikha government sanatorium.
The head of the Kremlin medical centre, Sergei Mironov, said Yeltsin would start meeting officials next week and would hold talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday.
Yeltsin would move from the Central Clinical Hospital to Barvikha permanently on Thursday or Friday, Mironov said in a television clip of the briefing for Russian media.

"The president's recuperation is going well. The president is active, Today he is going for a walk at the dacha in Barvikha, to be in normal surroundings for a while," Interfax news agency quoted Akchurin as saying.
Akchurin said Yeltsin, 65, had lost weight but had got stronger since the operation on November 5.

He also said that scarring on Yeltsin's heart revealed during the bypass surgery backed up his earlier view that the president had suffered a third, unannounced heart attack shortly before the run-off vote in which he won a second term.
A Russian newspaper on Saturday published the first picture of Yeltsin since the quintuple bypass operation to clear the blood supply problems which had led to the attacks.

The photograph, taking up much of the front page of the liberal daily Sevodnya, showed a relaxed-looking Yeltsin wearing an open-necked shirt and patterned cardigan drinking tea with his wife Naina and granddaugher Masha.
Sevodnya said the photograph, released by the presidential press service, was taken on Friday in the presidential wing of the hospital.
Later the press service said Yeltsin had worked four hours on Saturday on official papers, one hour longer than on Friday, and had signed a series of decrees.

Yeltsin has just completed the first 100 days of his second term in office, but his heart problems meant he has only been in the Kremlin a few times. Most of his time has been spent in Barvikha, a complex of government rest houses outside Moscow.
The picture seemed to be the latest step in the Kremlin's strategy of gradually preparing the 65-year-old president for a full public appearance.

Kremlin press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday a planned address to the nation, Yeltsin's first public act, was still being prepared. But he did not say when it would be. "You understand, the imagemakers want the president's appearance to have a big impact," he said.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted the doctors as saying on Sunday that the president was ready to address the nation at any time but that it was up to him to decide the date.
Yastrzhembsky had said on Tuesday that Yeltsin would address the nation within days, but did not specify whether this would be on television or radio.
